task.pr_title: Add built-in value converters for IPAddress

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description: Am not too sure about mapping IPAddress.None to null... None is a actually a valid value, equal to Broadcast (0x00000000FFFFFFFF).

evidence.thread_resolution:
ralmsdeveloper: @roji 
I agree with you, if you are not feeling well with `IPAddress.None` we can go from `IPAddress.Any` (_0.0.0.0_) this nullifies the possibility of having a Valid IP.

Let me know how you feel about it?


All right for you @ajcvickers
roji: @ralmsdeveloper I don't think IPAddress.Any is any more suitable than IPAddress.None - it's a valid IP value (in the sense that someone may need to store it). This would be the same as writing a value converter from int to string, where an int zero is converted to null: it would make it impossible to save a 0 to the database...

Is there any reason you think we need to convert any value to null?
roji: Note that IPAddress is a class (so nullable). I'd expect the value converter to convert a null IPAddress to a null byte[] and vice versa; I don't see a reason to convert any non-null value of IPAddress to null...
ralmsdeveloper: I'm working on it and I'll be back here in today!
ralmsdeveloper: @roji 
With the adjustments I made, we can now read and write a null value.
